record.paper_title: Opportunities and open questions in modern β decay
record.original_question: How can soft electromagnetic final-state interactions between beta-decay final-state particles be incorporated in a single consistent renormalization and matching framework accurate at the 0.01% level? The question includes how to reconcile the traditional Fermi-function treatment of Coulomb effects and radiative-correction factors with effective-field-theory treatments of running, matching, and large-logarithm resummation for neutron and finite-nuclear-charge beta decays.

evidence.quote: 3. How should one consistently include final state interactions to 0.01%-level precision?

Recently, however, this methodology is under scrutiny, as approaches using effective field theory find different results and stress the need for proper matching between scales in consistent renormalization schemes.
The exact correspondence for the neutron as well as for finite Z needs to be further investigated.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider allowed nuclear beta decay processes (in particular free neutron decay and beta decay of nuclei with finite nuclear charge Z) where one wishes to compute the differential and total decay rates with a theoretical uncertainty at or below the 10^{-4} (0.01%) level. The amplitude is dressed by soft electromagnetic final-state interactions between the outgoing charged particles (electron/positron, recoiling nucleus, and, where relevant, additional charged hadrons), which traditionally are encoded by (i) the Fermi function F(Z,E) resumming the Coulomb interaction between the lepton and the daughter nucleus, and (ii) multiplicative radiative-correction factors such as the outer correction g(E,E_0) and inner correction Δ_R^V capturing virtual and real soft photons.

Develop a single consistent renormalization and matching framework, formulated in the language of effective field theory (with a tower of EFTs separating the scales m_W, m_p, m_e, and the atomic/Coulomb scale Zα m_e), that:

1. Reproduces the established Fermi-function treatment of Coulomb effects in the appropriate low-energy limit, with controlled power counting in Zα and v/c.
2. Performs the matching of Wilson coefficients across each scale and resums the resulting large logarithms (e.g. log(m_W/m_p), log(m_p/m_e)) via renormalization-group evolution, in a scheme consistent with the definition of the Fermi function.
3. Yields a total theoretical uncertainty on the inclusive and differential rates that is demonstrably ≤ 0.01% for both the neutron (Z=0 daughter charge interpreted appropriately) and finite-Z nuclear cases, with all renormalization-scheme dependencies and double-counting between the Fermi function and EFT radiative corrections explicitly resolved.

Establish the exact correspondence between the traditional factorized form rate ∝ F(Z,E) · (1 + δ_R) · |M|^2 and the EFT factorization formula at this precision, for both the neutron and finite-Z beta decays.
artifact.category_tag: Effective field theory of beta decay
artifact.status_search_result: An EFT reformulation of the Fermi function ("Field Theory of the Fermi Function", Phys. Rev. Lett. 133, 021803, 2024) provides a factorization formula, matching at successive scales, and renormalization-group resummation of large logarithms, including a three-loop anomalous dimension. This addresses parts of the program for the neutron case, but the precise correspondence with the traditional Fermi-function/radiative-correction treatment at the 0.01% level, especially for finite nuclear charge Z, remains under active investigation and is not fully established.

status_evidence.title: Field Theory of the Fermi Function
status_evidence.snippet: The Fermi function is reformulated in EFT; factorization with matching coefficients and RG resummation of logarithms, with three-loop anomalous dimension.
status_evidence.claim: An EFT framework for the Fermi function with matching and log resummation now exists, addressing part of the question.

status_evidence.title: Field theory of the Fermi function (Fermilab preprint)
status_evidence.snippet: New factorization formula for QED radiative corrections to beta decays with EFT matching coefficients.
status_evidence.claim: The neutron / point-like case has been substantially advanced; finite-Z correspondence still needs further investigation.
